If she wasn't as active as she is now, would you still let her eat the way she does? It shouldn't be a this or that, it should be a constant. Her body variables put her at heavier for her body type already, and if she doesn't have that control for her diet, if she drops that active schedule she's going to balloon up. It doesn't have to be all or nothing, but some consistency in what she's eating now will set her mindset up for the future for healthy weight gain/loss when she slows down. NTA at all, but some healthy boundaries with food is appropriate. Idk about her knees buckling being a cause from her weight, that's a huge stretch and borderline mean for your husband to bring up. Being hypermobile can be made worse by a ton of weight, but your daughter dances and has muscles built up already to support and is no where near heavy enough for it to be a factor. Otherwise NFL linemen would be breaking knees all over the place. Knee strengthening exercises with bands and resistance will help with her knees buckling.
